intro: You lost a tooth. You found a worm. Your shoe fell in a puddle. Those are stories. They are true. They are yours. In this unit you learn to tell them so a reader can see them.
A story has a beginning, a middle and an end. It has order words. It has details. You will also write what you think and why. You will write a page of true facts. And you will fix your sentences.
Then you will say it out loud. Loud and clear. In order. With details. You will listen to others. You will ask questions. You will share your writing and hear what your friends think.
bigQuestion: How do you tell a true story so that someone else can see it and hear it?

timeline.t: Something small happens to you. A tooth comes out at lunch.
You close your eyes and see the moment again. Who? Where? What?
You draw three boxes: beginning, middle and end.
You write one line under each box, using first, next, then and last.
You add details a reader can see: the red apple, the wiggle.
You add a feeling word. You felt proud.
You fix your sentences: capital letter, spaces, a mark at the end.
You practice reading it loud and clear, with your chin up.
You sit in the author's chair and read it to the class.
You listen to two questions and add the best idea to your story.

test.q: Which part of a story tells how it turned out?
test.why: The end tells how the story turned out.

test.q: Leo did not know how to start. What helped him?
test.why: Leo drew three boxes. The pictures showed him what to write.

test.q: Which one is a small moment?
choices: The goat ate my map at the zoo
test.why: One short, true thing that happened to you is a small moment.

test.q: Which sentence is in the right order?
choices: First I ate. Then I woke up.
Last I woke up. First I ate.
First I woke up. Then I ate.
test.why: You wake up before you eat. First comes before then.

test.q: Which sentence has the most details?
choices: I had a small brown dog with a floppy ear.
test.why: Small, brown and floppy ear are details. They help the reader see the dog.

test.q: My favorite season is winter because I love to sled. What is the reason?
test.why: The word because opens the door to the reason: I love to sled.
Six legs is true for everyone. Best and scary are opinions.

test.q: What is wrong with this: the cat sat
choices: It needs a capital letter and an end mark
test.why: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a mark.

test.q: You do not understand what the teacher said. What do you do?
test.why: Asking is how you find out. It is smart.

choices: What I liked and what I wonder
test.why: Good feedback tells what you liked and what you wonder about.

write.prompt: Pick one small moment that really happened to you. Tell it so a reader can see it. Then tell why it is a good story to share.
tips: Say your claim: This is a good story to share because...
Give it a beginning, a middle and an end. Use first, next, then and last.
Add two details a reader can see and one feeling word.
Check each sentence: capital letter, spaces, a mark at the end.
Read it out loud to someone. Ask what they liked and what they wonder.
